newsitem.title: USA: US metal premiums steady, aluminum scrap firms up.
newsitem.headline: US metal premiums steady, aluminum scrap firms up.

text.p: Base metal premiums in the United States remained largely unchanged from last week, but zinc has eased off a touch from its recent high, traders said.
Zinc premiums are still strong and quoted at 5.50 to 5.75 cents per pound over LME cash, with the upper end off some 0.25 cent from last week.
The market was still physically tight, traders said.
"The only thing that's keeping the U.S. market together are the imports, and I don't think there is an unlimited amount coming in," a producer-linked dealer said.
Traders said aluminum premiums were also stable with March delivery quoted at 5.25 to 5.50 cents per pound over LME cash, though some believed the upper end of the range may be softer than last week.
Aluminum premiums were quoted at 5.00 to 5.25 cents for the second quarter and about 4.5 cents for the second half of the year.
"I think people talked up the premiums last week because there was a bit of panic with the lead times going out and out," a merchant said.
With a surge in LME aluminum prices, scrap prices have inevitably begun to move higher with the main grades up by 2 to 3 cents a pound.

"The alloy prices are going to have to start firming up with the run up in scrap. I am anticipating there is going to be a rise in A380 alloy prices to 78 cents a lb later this week," a Midwest alloy smelter source said.
Midwest alloy was about 76 cents per pound at the moment.
Tin premiums were still languishing with little change from the recent softness.

Physical nickel traders offered differing views on the market, with some noting firmer premiums in the 13 to 15 cents per pound range over LME cash for melting grade metal, with small lots fetching up to 18 cents.
But others pegged premiums lower at 9 to 11 cents.

"When the market dipped, a couple of consumers bought small lots, but now it's over $8,000 per tonne, buying has turned off for the time being," a dealer said. "But I know a lot of people will need material in two to three weeks time."
LME three months nickel prices surged $200 higher to $8,190 a tonne Wednesday.
Some traders believed the strength in LME nickel was largely due to fund investment seeking to make a buck out of a possible strike at Norilsk Nickel plant in Russia.
But others countered that strength in nickel was "underpinned by very firm aggressive demand."
